義大利吉他為魯特形撥弦樂器，調音近似吉他，文藝復興時期在義大利常見。Renato: The chitarra italiana is a lute-shaped plucked instrument tuned much as the guitar is and common in Renaissance Italy. Renato Meucci notes that the name italiana appeared after the flat-backed chitarra alla spagnola reached Italy, to distinguish the two versions. The source says it may derive from the panduras of the ancient Mediterranean and is related to the North African kwitra. Its bass variant, the chitarrone, existed from the thirteenth to the eighteenth century and became rarer later; Laurence Wright noted in 1976 that chitarrone means large guitar, that it has a round back, that it is easily taken for a smaller lute, and that it was occasionally confused with the mandola when the mandola was popular.
義大利吉他的琵琶形共鳴箱通常採用雲杉或樅木製作面板，背板與側板則多用楓木、桃花心: The lute-shaped resonator of the chitarra italiana usually has a soundboard of spruce or fir, with the back and sides of hardwood such as maple, mahogany or walnut. The neck is hard maple or ash, and the fingerboard ebony. The strings were originally of gut and were later changed to nylon or metal. The head and tuning pegs may be inlaid with bone, ivory or shell, showing the refinement of Renaissance craft.
義大利吉他音色清亮明淨，具有琵琶般的穿透力與溫潤的撥弦質感。其音域偏中高，音色相: The chitarra italiana has a clear, bright timbre, with the carrying quality of a lute and a warm plucked texture. Its range lies on the high side of the middle, and its tone is relatively light and nimble, not as heavy and round as the modern classical guitar. Because it uses single or double strings, each note resonates more independently and more finely, with the elegant character of the Renaissance.
與西班牙吉他相比，義大利版本音色更顯清透細緻；與琵琶相比，則少了東方樂器的蒼涼感: Compared with the Spanish guitar, the Italian version sounds clearer and more delicate; compared with the pipa, it lacks the bleakness of an Eastern instrument and has more of a cheerful European classical character. Its resonance depends on the special structure of the lute-shaped body, which produces a sound that is neither over-inflated nor thin, and suits Renaissance chamber playing.
